Lines.Text: starting beneath the spot button , use the round side of the metal spudger and firmly pry underneath the grey top panel of the camera . work your way counterclockwise around the camera prying at different spots until the top panel starts to come loose . pry all the way around until you reach the stsi logo .
this prying will not completely release the top cover . it is also necessary to take off the side panel , as explained in the next step .

Steps.Text_raw: Starting beneath the "SPOT" button, use the round side of the metal spudger and firmly pry underneath the grey top panel of the camera. Work your way counterclockwise around the camera prying at different spots until the top panel starts to come loose. Pry all the way around until you reach the "STsi" logo. This prying will not completely release the top cover. It is also necessary to take off the side panel, as explained in the next step.

Lines.Text: be careful when removing the right side panel . there is a plastic component underneath the side panel that will come free . note the orientation of this plastic component for reassembly because it is connected to the back-cover release switch .
also be gentle when removing the top panel because it is delicate and is connected by wires .
carefully remove the right side panel by grasping it at the bottom and rotating is counter-clockwise . the top panel is now free to snap off .

Steps.Text_raw: Be careful when removing the right side panel. There is a plastic component underneath the side panel that will come free. Note the orientation of this plastic component for reassembly because it is connected to the back-cover release switch. Also be gentle when removing the top panel because it is delicate and is connected by wires. Carefully remove the right side panel by grasping it at the bottom and rotating is counter-clockwise. The top panel is now free to snap off.

Lines.Text: remove the two black phillips 00 5.0 mm screws on the viewfinder panel to take off the viewfinder .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the two black Phillips #00 5.0 mm screws on the viewfinder panel to take off the viewfinder.

there's a little silver bracket that is held down by the phillips 00 screw so be careful not to lose it .
with a little prying , use the spudger to detach the media adapter's connector from the motherboard .

Title: Repairing Sigma 8-16 mm lens

Lines.Text: fantastic little aps-c format lens . note the big bulbous front element .

Steps.Text_raw: Fantastic little APS-C format lens. Note the big bulbous front element.

Lines.Text: there are a guhzillion tiny screws and pieces in this lens . get a bunch of ziplock baggies to hold each piece and its screws . trust me on this .

Steps.Text_raw: There are a guhzillion tiny screws and pieces in this lens. Get a bunch of ziplock baggies to hold each piece and its screws. Trust me on this.

Lines.Text: remove the four screws holding the black center piece . there's one screw that sticks out a bit - no need to remove that one .
remove the central black piece . the camera connector plate will hang loose for a while .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the four screws holding the black center piece. There's one screw that sticks out a bit - no need to remove that one. Remove the central black piece. The camera connector plate will hang loose for a while.

Lines.Text: remove the four screws holding the mounting plate . lift off the mounting plate . ( photo shows inner components in place . )
remove the four spacer rings below the mounting plate . be careful not to bend the brass rings .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the four screws holding the mounting plate. Lift off the mounting plate. (Photo shows inner components in place.) Remove the four spacer rings below the mounting plate. Be careful not to bend the brass rings.

Lines.Text: unscrew the two screws holding the focus switch plate . the plate should just fall off .

Steps.Text_raw: Unscrew the two screws holding the focus switch plate. The plate should just fall off.

Lines.Text: there is one screw securing the top cover . remove the screw and lift off the cover .

Steps.Text_raw: There is one screw securing the top cover. Remove the screw and lift off the cover.

Lines.Text: the ribbon cables are inserted into easy click connectors . ''carefully'' pull out the retaining sliders and remove the cables .
remove the one screw holding the autofocus switch . remove the switch . it's sticky on the back so it will take a bit of levering .

Steps.Text_raw: The ribbon cables are inserted into easy click connectors. ''Carefully'' pull out the retaining sliders and remove the cables. Remove the one screw holding the autofocus switch. Remove the switch. It's sticky on the back so it will take a bit of levering.

Lines.Text: unscrew the two screws securing the circuit board . remove the board .

Steps.Text_raw: Unscrew the two screws securing the circuit board. Remove the board.

Lines.Text: remove the rubber grip around the zoom ring .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the rubber grip around the zoom ring.

Lines.Text: peel off the copper tape covering the zoom encoder fingers .
unscrew and remove the zoom encoder fingers . ''be careful'' - these fingers are very delicate .

Steps.Text_raw: Peel off the copper tape covering the zoom encoder fingers. Unscrew and remove the zoom encoder fingers. ''Be careful'' - these fingers are very delicate.

Lines.Text: remove the screw deep inside the brass zoom stop . grab the zoom stop with tweezers . wiggle it until it comes free .
if you want , or need to , you can remove the zoom ring . rotate it and gently pull up until it pops off . leave it in place if you can to prevent damage to the encoder .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the screw deep inside the brass zoom stop. Grab the zoom stop with tweezers. Wiggle it until it comes free. If you want, or need to, you can remove the zoom ring. Rotate it and gently pull up until it pops off. Leave it in place if you can to prevent damage to the encoder.

Lines.Text: in case you're interested ( and admit it , you are ) there is no screw underneath the pretty sigma dg sticker .

Steps.Text_raw: In case you're interested (and admit it, you are) there is no screw underneath the pretty SIGMA DG sticker.

Lines.Text: remove the three screws around the outer ring . lift off the zoom ring assembly . ''don't snag the ribbon cables . ''

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the three screws around the outer ring. Lift off the zoom ring assembly. ''Don't snag the ribbon cables.''

Lines.Text: if the lens takes a hard hit , it is this zoom assembly that will probably break . in my case a couple of the support studs snapped off .
glue any broken pieces with strongest epoxy glue you can find . superglue is probably not a good choice because it won't handle any lateral knocks .
be careful not to get glue where you don't want it . use tape to keep the glue in place .
put some weight on the assembly while the glue dries so that the repaired studs stay in position . if they are raised , even slightly , the lens alignment will be off .

Steps.Text_raw: If the lens takes a hard hit, it is this zoom assembly that will probably break . In my case a couple of the support studs snapped off. Glue any broken pieces with strongest epoxy glue you can find. Superglue is probably not a good choice because it won't handle any lateral knocks. Be careful not to get glue where you don't want it. Use tape to keep the glue in place. Put some weight on the assembly while the glue dries so that the repaired studs stay in position. If they are raised, even slightly, the lens alignment will be off.

Lines.Text: try not to get glue down the outer side of the support stud . excess glue will interfere with reassembly later . if glue does get in the wrong place , carefully grind it down with a dremel tool once it hardens .

Steps.Text_raw: Try not to get glue down the outer side of the support stud. Excess glue will interfere with reassembly later. If glue does get in the wrong place, carefully grind it down with a dremel tool once it hardens.

Lines.Text: the next step will free the lens unit from the focus barrel . if you don't properly support that big , bulbous , expensive front element it will fall ''clunk'' to the table top .

take a blob of plasticine or playdough about the size of a tangerine . stick it into a baggie ( baggies are your friend ! ) and mold it into a flattened ball with a dent about the size and shape of that big front element .

take a clean lens cloth and lay it on top of the baggie . nestle your lens into the dent . the plasticine should support the entire lens off the table . i . e . , the lens hood should not be touching the table .

Steps.Text_raw: The next step will free the lens unit from the focus barrel. If you don't properly support that big, bulbous, expensive front element it will fall ''clunk'' to the table top. Take a blob of plasticine or playdough about the size of a tangerine. Stick it into a baggie (baggies are your friend!) and mold it into a flattened ball with a dent about the size and shape of that big front element. Take a clean lens cloth and lay it on top of the baggie. Nestle your lens into the dent. The plasticine should support the entire lens off the table. I.e., the lens hood should not be touching the table.

Lines.Text: the screws holding these pieces together are in there very tightly . make sure your screwdriver has sufficient 'bite' or you will strip the head ( and then you're in deep trouble ) . you may also have to push down quite a bit to get the screws to turn . find a friend to hold the lens steady while you do this .
unscrew the five screws around the top of the light gray ring . this will free the lens unit from the focus barrel .
put a tab of masking tape , or an elastic band , on the lens hood ( ''not the focus ring'' ) . mark the location of the ribbon cable . this will save you much grief during reassembly .

Steps.Text_raw: The screws holding these pieces together are in there very tightly. Make sure your screwdriver has sufficient 'bite' or you will strip the head (and then you're in deep trouble). You may also have to push down quite a bit to get the screws to turn. Find a friend to hold the lens steady while you do this. Unscrew the five screws around the top of the light gray ring. This will free the lens unit from the focus barrel. Put a tab of masking tape, or an elastic band, on the lens hood (''not the focus ring''). Mark the location of the ribbon cable. This will save you much grief during reassembly.

Lines.Text: ''danger ! '' your autofocus may never work again if you proceed past this point .

remove the four screws from the inner base of the zoom ring housing . they will require some torque to get them out . make sure your screwdriver has enough 'bite' and push down while turning . get your friend back in to hold the barrel steady .
the housing will try to spring up ; unscrew the screws evenly and apply some downward pressure on the housing as you remove the screws .

Steps.Text_raw: ''Danger!'' Your autofocus may never work again if you proceed past this point. Remove the four screws from the inner base of the zoom ring housing. They will require some torque to get them out. Make sure your screwdriver has enough 'bite' and push down while turning. Get your friend back in to hold the barrel steady. The housing will try to spring up; unscrew the screws evenly and apply some downward pressure on the housing as you remove the screws.

Lines.Text: remove all of the rings up to , but not including , the one with the f stop labels . it won't come off - don't force it .
with a small tipped tool , remove two of the three impossibly small plastic tabs from the barrel . don't remove the one behind the f-stop label - it's a right pain to put back in .
remove the remaining rings including the brass clutch plates .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove all of the rings up to, but not including, the one with the F stop labels. It won't come off - don't force it. With a small tipped tool, remove two of the three impossibly small plastic tabs from the barrel. Don't remove the one behind the F-stop label - it's a right pain to put back in. Remove the remaining rings including the brass clutch plates.

Lines.Text: remove the rubber focus grip . the focus grip is not interchangeable with the zoom grip . the focus grip has slightly finer fingers .
remove the three screws and their bearings from the focus ring .
pull the focus ring straight up to remove .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the rubber focus grip. The focus grip is not interchangeable with the zoom grip. The focus grip has slightly finer "fingers". Remove the three screws and their bearings from the focus ring. Pull the focus ring straight up to remove.

Lines.Text: this teardown doesn't go any further . go ahead and disassemble the lens unit if you dare .
reassembly is tricky ; the remaining steps will help you put it back together again .

Steps.Text_raw: This teardown doesn't go any further. Go ahead and disassemble the lens unit if you dare. Reassembly is tricky; the remaining steps will help you put it back together again.

Lines.Text: drop on the focus ring and replace the screws and bearings . flip the bearing rings so that they nestle into the screws .
slip on the rubber focus grip . use the one with the finer ribs .

Steps.Text_raw: Drop on the focus ring and replace the screws and bearings. Flip the bearing rings so that they nestle into the screws. Slip on the rubber focus grip. Use the one with the finer ribs.

Lines.Text: the order of assembly , from bottom to top is :

steel/plastic , brass clutch plates , focus indicator , black plastic , thin rubber , rotor ( thick black ) , stator ( funky brass thing with a ribbon cable ) , fiber , split steel , fiber , steel ( no split ) , thick brass , thin brass , spring .

Steps.Text_raw: The order of assembly, from bottom to top is: Steel/plastic, brass clutch plates, focus indicator, black plastic, thin rubber, rotor (thick black), stator (funky brass thing with a ribbon cable), fiber, split steel, fiber, steel (no split), thick brass, thin brass, spring.

Lines.Text: insert the ring that is steel on one side and black plastic on the other . plastic side goes down . engage the tabs into the focus ring .
drop in the clutch plates and engage the inner tabs into the central barrel . be careful not to lose the tiny ball bearings in the plates .

Steps.Text_raw: Insert the ring that is steel on one side and black plastic on the other. Plastic side goes down. Engage the tabs into the focus ring. Drop in the clutch plates and engage the inner tabs into the central barrel. Be careful not to lose the tiny ball bearings in the plates.

Lines.Text: drop on the focus indicator ring . there are shallow indents on the bottom that engage the tabs on the bearing plates . ( shown here in an assembled state . )
the ring can go on two ways . make sure the numbers are on the same side as that mark you made earlier .

Steps.Text_raw: Drop on the focus indicator ring. There are shallow indents on the bottom that engage the tabs on the bearing plates. (Shown here in an assembled state.) The ring can go on two ways. Make sure the numbers are on the same side as that mark you made earlier.

Lines.Text: drop on the black plastic ring and rubber ring . the rubber ring should nestle nicely into the plastic ring .
the focus label should be on the same side as the mark on the lens hood .
the rotor is the moving part of the ultrasonic wave motor . it's the metal ring that's black on one side , shiny on the other . drop it on with the shiny side down . ( sorry , no picture . )

Steps.Text_raw: Drop on the black plastic ring and rubber ring . The rubber ring should nestle nicely into the plastic ring. The focus label should be on the same side as the mark on the lens hood. The rotor is the moving part of the ultrasonic wave motor. It's the metal ring that's black on one side, shiny on the other. Drop it on with the shiny side down. (Sorry, no picture.)

Lines.Text: the stator is the fixed half of the ultrasonic wave motor .
insert the impossibly small plastic tabs into the main barrel . these hold the stator in the correct position .
drop on the stator with the wire pointing up . there are indents on the inside that line up with the impossibly small plastic tabs .
the stator will go on three ways . make sure the ribbon cable aligns with the mark you made earlier .

Steps.Text_raw: The stator is the fixed half of the ultrasonic wave motor. Insert the impossibly small plastic tabs into the main barrel. These hold the stator in the correct position. Drop on the stator with the wire pointing up. There are indents on the inside that line up with the impossibly small plastic tabs. The stator will go on three ways. Make sure the ribbon cable aligns with the mark you made earlier.

Lines.Text: drop on the remaining rings in this order :
fiber ring , split metal ring ( it has a little tab that engages into the barrel ) , the other fiber ring , solid metal ring , brass rings , spring . ( apologies for the crap picture . )

Steps.Text_raw: Drop on the remaining rings in this order: Fiber ring, split metal ring (it has a little tab that engages into the barrel), the other fiber ring, solid metal ring, brass rings, spring. (Apologies for the crap picture.)

Lines.Text: drop on the metal zoom barrel . secure with the four screws .

Steps.Text_raw: Drop on the metal zoom barrel. Secure with the four screws.

Lines.Text: drop the focus assembly onto the main lens module . be careful with the ribbon cables .
align the five screw holes . secure with screws .

Steps.Text_raw: Drop the focus assembly onto the main lens module. Be careful with the ribbon cables. Align the five screw holes. Secure with screws.

Lines.Text: drop on the zoom assembly . carefully thread the focus encoder cable through the slot .
align the screw holes and secure .

Steps.Text_raw: Drop on the zoom assembly. Carefully thread the focus encoder cable through the slot. Align the screw holes and secure.

Lines.Text: rotate the zoom ring until the oval hole lines up with its mate on the lens module . insert brass pin and secure with a screw .
reattach the zoom encoder fingers and copper tape .
replace the rubber zoom grip .

Steps.Text_raw: Rotate the zoom ring until the oval hole lines up with its mate on the lens module. Insert brass pin and secure with a screw. Reattach the zoom encoder fingers and copper tape. Replace the rubber zoom grip.

Lines.Text: reinstall the circuit board with the two screws .
replace the zoom switch .
insert all ribbon cables and firmly ( but carefully ) click the connectors in to place .
insert the camera connector cable and click the connector .

Steps.Text_raw: Reinstall the circuit board with the two screws. Replace the zoom switch. Insert all ribbon cables and firmly (but carefully) click the connectors in to place. Insert the camera connector cable and click the connector.

Lines.Text: drop on the top cover and align with the screw holes . the large side fits over the zoom switch .
secure with one screw . the screw hole is slightly deeper than the other holes .

Steps.Text_raw: Drop on the top cover and align with the screw holes. The large side fits over the zoom switch. Secure with one screw. The screw hole is slightly deeper than the other holes.

Lines.Text: make sure the interior and exterior zoom switches are in the same position . they must line up when you replace the cover .
replace the zoom switch cover and secure with two screws .

Steps.Text_raw: Make sure the interior and exterior zoom switches are in the same position. They must line up when you replace the cover. Replace the zoom switch cover and secure with two screws.

Lines.Text: replace the spacer rings . the brass rings go on the bottom , the thickest black ring is on top . the rings fit onto a tab that keeps them aligned . make sure the holes line up with the screw holes in assembly below .
drop on the mounting plate . the long leg goes inside the lens and into a hole in the central lens assembly ; it's easy to see .
secure the mounting plate with four screws . the shorter screw is directly opposite the red dot .

Steps.Text_raw: Replace the spacer rings. The brass rings go on the bottom, the thickest black ring is on top. The rings fit onto a tab that keeps them aligned. Make sure the holes line up with the screw holes in assembly below. Drop on the mounting plate. The long leg goes inside the lens and into a hole in the central lens assembly; it's easy to see. Secure the mounting plate with four screws. The shorter screw is directly opposite the red dot.

Lines.Text: attach the camera connector plate with two screws . these screws have a finer thread than the others .
insert the black center piece . secure with the remaining two coarse-thread screws .

Steps.Text_raw: Attach the camera connector plate with two screws. These screws have a finer thread than the others. Insert the black center piece. Secure with the remaining two coarse-thread screws.

Title: How to Adjust the Mobius ActionCam Camera Focus

Lines.Text: use a phillips 00 screwdriver to remove both screws on the bottom of the case .
use a box cutter or knife to split the quality control seal on the front of the device .
be aware that breaking the seal will probably void any warranty .

Steps.Text_raw: Use a Phillips #00 screwdriver to remove both screws on the bottom of the case. Use a box cutter or knife to split the quality control seal on the front of the device. Be aware that breaking the seal will probably void any warranty.

Lines.Text: pull the casing apart near the lens .
slide back the bottom half of the case to disengage the clips holding the casing halves together .
gently remove the bottom of the case and place it alongside the device .
the battery pack is mounted to the bottom casing . be gentle when opening the case to avoid damaging the harness that runs from the battery to the circuit board .

Steps.Text_raw: Pull the casing apart near the lens. Slide back the bottom half of the case to disengage the clips holding the casing halves together. Gently remove the bottom of the case and place it alongside the device. The battery pack is mounted to the bottom casing. Be gentle when opening the case to avoid damaging the harness that runs from the battery to the circuit board.

Lines.Text: locate the camera module .
grab the sides of the camera module and gently pull to free it from the case .
be gentle when handling the camera module to avoid damaging the fragile ribbon cable attached to it .

Steps.Text_raw: Locate the camera module. Grab the sides of the camera module and gently pull to free it from the case. Be gentle when handling the camera module to avoid damaging the fragile ribbon cable attached to it.

Lines.Text: use a 0.9 mm hex key or driver to loosen the set screw fastened into the side of the camera module .
loosen the screw until it turns freely . do not fully remove the set screw .

Steps.Text_raw: Use a 0.9mm hex key or driver to loosen the set screw fastened into the side of the camera module. Loosen the screw until it turns freely. Do not fully remove the set screw.

Lines.Text: grab the side of the lens and gently turn to adjust the focus .

while facing the back of the camera module , turning the lens all the way clockwise will bring objects 4-6 away into focus . turning the lens all the way counterclockwise will bring distant objects into focus .
the lens has about a half turn of travel .

Steps.Text_raw: Grab the side of the lens and gently turn to adjust the focus. While facing the back of the camera module, turning the lens all the way clockwise will bring objects 4"-6" away into focus. Turning the lens all the way counterclockwise will bring distant objects into focus. The lens has about a half turn of travel.

Lines.Text: use a phillips 00 screwdriver to remove both screws on the bottom of the case .
use a box cutter or knife to split the quality control seal on the front of the device .
be aware that breaking the seal will probably void any warranty .

Steps.Text_raw: Use a Phillips #00 screwdriver to remove both screws on the bottom of the case. Use a box cutter or knife to split the quality control seal on the front of the device. Be aware that breaking the seal will probably void any warranty.

Lines.Text: pull the casing apart near the lens .
slide back the bottom half of the case to disengage the clips holding the casing halves together .
gently remove the bottom of the case and place it alongside the device .
the battery pack is mounted to the bottom casing . be gentle when opening the case to avoid damaging the harness that runs from the battery to the circuit board .

Steps.Text_raw: Pull the casing apart near the lens. Slide back the bottom half of the case to disengage the clips holding the casing halves together. Lines.Text: locate the camera module .
grab the sides of the camera module and gently pull upwards to free it from the case .
be gentle when handling the camera module to avoid damaging the fragile ribbon cable attached to it .
use your finger to pull up the black tab on the rear of the ribbon cable connector .
slide the ribbon cable out of the connector to remove the camera module .
when plugging the ribbon cable back into the connector the copper pads face upwards .

Steps.Text_raw: Locate the camera module. Grab the sides of the camera module and gently pull upwards to free it from the case. Be gentle when handling the camera module to avoid damaging the fragile ribbon cable attached to it. Use your finger to pull up the black tab on the rear of the ribbon cable connector. Slide the ribbon cable out of the connector to remove the camera module. When plugging the ribbon cable back into the connector the copper pads face upwards.

Lines.Text: grab the battery plug with a pair of small needle nose pliers . gently pull upwards to disengage the connectors .
be gentle when removing the plug to avoid damaging the battery cable .
if the board mounted battery connector housing comes loose it can simply be pushed back on to the terminal pins .
lift up one end of the battery . '''slowly''' pull the battery off the adhesive backing .

Steps.Text_raw: Grab the battery plug with a pair of small needle nose pliers. Gently pull upwards to disengage the connectors. Be gentle when removing the plug to avoid damaging the battery cable. If the board mounted battery connector housing comes loose it can simply be pushed back on to the terminal pins. Lift up one end of the battery. '''Slowly''' pull the battery off the adhesive backing.

Lines.Text: locate the 3 screws securing the circuit board to the casing .
use a phillips 1 screwdriver to remove the screws .
lift the edge of the circuit board up . slide the circuit board out of the casing .

Steps.Text_raw: Locate the 3 screws securing the circuit board to the casing. Use a Phillips #1 screwdriver to remove the screws. Lift the edge of the circuit board up. Slide the circuit board out of the casing.

Lines.Text: remove the interface buttons from the top of the case .
remove the circuit board backing material .

Lines.Text: yeah , insides . really technical term .

to remove the internal module of main board , usb connector board , lens , and lens surround ( now you know why i just called it insides . ) , you will need to loosen the cyanoacrylate and the hot glue .

luckily , the cyanoacrylate doesn't bond well to the aluminum shell , so a firm hit on the lens surround should probably loosen it up . my camera had already experienced a fall , so i assume it had loosened then , not to mention i really took it apart another , less optimal way .

loosening the hot glue is simply a matter of heating it up again . heat the upper front sides of the shell with whatever heat source you have . i used a small butane torch , but you can probably use a hot air gun even though it diesn't have as fine of control , or a hot air soldering machine ( pictured ) .
while heating the outside of the shell , push on the main board from the back until you feel it slip , and push everything out the front .
needless to say , be careful not to melt the lens surround . if you've got it that hot , the hot glue melted long ago .

if you think you've melted the hot glue but the main board is still not budging , press ( or hit ) the lens surround back in towards the center of the camera to try to jar the cyanoacrylate loose , being careful about the hot aluminum .

Steps.Text_raw: Yeah, "insides." Really technical term. To remove the internal module of main board, USB connector board, lens, and lens surround (now you know why I just called it "insides."), you will need to loosen the cyanoacrylate and the hot glue. Luckily, the cyanoacrylate doesn't bond well to the aluminum shell, so a firm hit on the lens surround should probably loosen it up. My camera had already experienced a fall, so I assume it had loosened then, not to mention I really took it apart another, less optimal way. Loosening the hot glue is simply a matter of heating it up again. Heat the upper front sides of the shell with whatever heat source you have. I used a small butane torch, but you can probably use a hot air gun even though it diesn't have as fine of control, or a hot air soldering machine (pictured). While heating the outside of the shell, push on the main board from the back until you feel it slip, and push everything out the front. Needless to say, be careful not to melt the lens surround. If you've got it that hot, the hot glue melted long ago. If you think you've melted the hot glue but the main board is still not budging, press (or hit) the lens surround  back in towards the center of the camera to try to jar the cyanoacrylate loose, being careful about the hot aluminum.

Lines.Text: look at the main board . does anything look wrong or discolored ? maybe there's a problem there . in my case , there was corrosion from water damage in various places . but what was really damaged ?

even though the battery voltage measured a reasonable 3.6 volts , it was dead . temporarily wiring in a fully charged battery ( you do have spare lithium ion batteries around , don't you ? ) revealed one particularly hot component . yes , be careful when touching components on the main board , and look and smell for telltale signs of smoke or overheating .
once you figure which component may be bad , remove and replace it . if you don't have any replacement , still remove it and test just to see how well it can limp by without it .

in my case , i removed one component , but it was actually an adjacent capacitor that was getting really hot . removing that capacitor brought some functionality back- the leds actually lit . replacing the original component and putting in a new capacitor brought everything back again .

Steps.Text_raw: Look at the main board. Does anything look wrong or discolored? Maybe there's a problem there. In my case, there was corrosion from water damage in various places. But what was really damaged? Even though the battery voltage measured a reasonable 3.6 volts, it was dead. Temporarily wiring in a fully charged battery (you do have spare lithium ion batteries around, don't you?) revealed one particularly hot component. Yes, be careful when touching components on the main board, and look and smell for telltale signs of smoke or overheating. Once you figure which component may be bad, remove and replace it. If you don't have any replacement, still remove it and test just to see how well it can limp by without it. In my case, I removed one component, but it was actually an adjacent capacitor that was getting really hot. Removing that capacitor brought some functionality back- the LEDs actually lit. Replacing the original component and putting in a new capacitor brought everything back again.

Lines.Text: to reinstall the main board , apply hot glue to the front corners of the main board . if you try to apply glue to the inside of the shell , the glue will be pressed in along the tracks and harden up before you can push the main board all the way in .
if you do it quickly enough , you can apply the hot glue and insert the main board before the hot glue hardens up . otherwise heat up the shell again to soften the hot glue .

optionally , you can apply either hot glue , or silicone caulk or cement to the inside edges of the lens surround . silicone is easier since it will not set while you're pressing it in . with hot glue you will need to heat the whole front part of the shell .
you may also use cyanoacrylate on the lens surround since it's more easily available , but it is less waterproof and less flexible .

this still does not waterproof the front assembly- the lens is only friction fit into the lens surround . it may or may not be waterproof , and waterproofing the camera is beyond the scope of this guide .
the purpose of gluing in the lens surround is to cut down on the torque the usb connector board experiences as the battery presses on it from the back .

Steps.Text_raw: To reinstall the main board, apply hot glue to the front corners of the main board. If you try to apply glue to the inside of the shell, the glue will be pressed in along the tracks and harden up before you can push the main board all the way in. If you do it quickly enough, you can apply the hot glue and insert the main board before the hot glue hardens up. Otherwise heat up the shell again to soften the hot glue. Optionally, you can apply either hot glue, or silicone caulk or cement to the inside edges of the lens surround. Silicone is easier since it will not set while you're pressing it in. With hot glue you will need to heat the whole front part of the shell. You may also use cyanoacrylate on the lens surround since it's more easily available, but it is less waterproof and less flexible. This still does not waterproof the front assembly- the lens is only friction fit into the lens surround. It may or may not be waterproof, and waterproofing the camera is beyond the scope of this guide. The purpose of gluing in the lens surround is to cut down on the torque the USB connector board experiences as the battery presses on it from the back.

Lines.Text: this is a camera produced by a japanese camera manufacturer . the japanese camera industry loves using ( japanese industrial standard ) screws .

Steps.Text_raw: This is a camera produced by a Japanese camera manufacturer. The Japanese camera industry loves using [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Industrial_Standards|JIS] (Japanese Industrial Standard) screws. Don't be tempted by your Phillips screw driver collection. Although PH#00 will interchange with JIS#00, it is not a perfect fit. Using Phillips will cause more wear on the head of the JIS screws and cause the screws to prematurely strip. Have both JIS#00 and JIS#000 screw drivers available for this teardown. Steps.Text_raw: This is a camera produced by a Japanese camera manufacturer. The Japanese camera industry loves using [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Industrial_Standards|JIS] (Japanese Industrial Standard) screws. Don't be tempted by your Phillips screw driver collection. Although PH#00 will interchange with JIS#00, it is not a perfect fit. Lines.Text: remove the battery and memory card from the device .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the battery and memory card from the device.

Lines.Text: remove 2 ( 0.3 mm ) screws from the left side of the camera .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove 2 (0.3mm) screws from the left side of the camera.

Lines.Text: remove 4 ( 0.3 mm ) screws from the right side of the camera .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove 4 (0.3mm) screws from the right side of the camera.

Lines.Text: remove 3 ( 0.4 mm ) screws from the base of the camera .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove 3 (0.4mm) screws from the base of the camera.

Lines.Text: arrange your screws properly .

Steps.Text_raw: Arrange your screws properly.

Lines.Text: do not remove the rear casing because it is attached via cable to the main pcb and circuit board .
pry the casing upward slightly , careful not to remove it . only lift it slightly as shown in the picture .

the lcd is attached to the rear casing via a light coating of adhesive on the underside of the yellow highlighted area . in the next step you will apply light pressure to the lcd to release it from the case .

Steps.Text_raw: Do not remove the Rear Casing because it is attached via cable to the Main PCB and circuit board. Pry the casing upward slightly, careful NOT to remove it.  Only lift it slightly as shown in the picture. The LCD is attached to the rear casing via a light coating of adhesive on the underside of the yellow highlighted area. In the next step you will apply light pressure to the LCD to release it from the case.

Lines.Text: do not apply heavy pressure and do not apply uneven pressure . if you find yourself applying too much pressure then dab some isopropyl alcohol 91 using a qtip along the edges to loosen the adhesive .
using your thumbs gently apply pressure to release the lcd . both thumbs should be applying even pressure and work your way down to the bottom .
once lcd is free of casing , remove rear case .

Steps.Text_raw: Do not apply heavy pressure and Do Not apply uneven pressure.  If you find yourself applying too much pressure then dab some Isopropyl Alcohol 91% using a qtip along the edges to loosen the adhesive. Using your thumbs gently apply pressure to release the LCD.  Both thumbs should be applying even pressure and work your way down to the bottom. Once LCD is free of casing, remove Rear Case.

Lines.Text: flip the black clamp to the open ( up ) position using a spudger or other method .
pull out the flex cable from the clamp using flat needle nose pliers or other method .

Steps.Text_raw: Flip the black clamp to the open (up) position using a spudger or other method. Pull out the flex cable from the clamp using flat needle nose pliers or other method.

Lines.Text: use a spudger or other tool to release the plastic hold down . then pry the entire assembly upward releasing it from the socket . try to keep the part as level as possible while prying up .
remove the part
in the last picture you can see ( on the reverse side of the part ) the socket . this helps understand how the socket snaps down onto the main board .

Steps.Text_raw: Use a Spudger or other tool to release the plastic hold down. Then pry the entire assembly upward releasing it from the socket.  Try to keep the part as level as possible while prying up. Remove the part In the last picture you can see (on the reverse side of the part) the socket. This helps understand how the  socket snaps down onto the Main Board.

Lines.Text: remove 3 silver ( 0.8 mm ) screws from the rear metal plate .
lift up and remove the metal plate

Steps.Text_raw: Remove 3 silver (0.8mm) screws from the rear metal plate. Lift up and remove the metal plate

Lines.Text: use the spudger or other tool to flip up the lcd cable clamp .
use needle nose pliers or other tool to pull out the cable from the clamp .

note : the metal protection plate has been removed so do not let the lcd rest on the rear of the camera . do not touch any part of the rear camera or circuits with your bare hands . esd can destroy your camera .
remove the lcd part vyk4 p64
when you purchase part make sure it has all three components included ( backlite , touch screen and lcd display )

Steps.Text_raw: Use the spudger or other tool to flip up the LCD cable clamp. Use Needle nose pliers or other tool to pull out the cable from the clamp. Note: The metal protection plate has been removed so DO NOT let the LCD rest on the Rear of the camera. Do NOT touch any part of the rear camera or circuits with your bare hands. ESD can destroy your camera. Remove the LCD part VYK4P64 When you purchase part make sure it has all three components included (backlite, touch screen and LCD display)

the bottom covering is attached by a hinge . removing this part will also require a small amount of force to separate .

after the part is fully away from the camera , move the part downward and out . it should now be fully extended and able to bend at the band that is attached to the body .
do not remove the control wheel panel from the camera . simply move to the side in order to access the orange band holding the lcd screen to the motherboard .

Lines.Text: set the lcd screen to the side

do not pull the white strip on top of the orange band . this is part of the circuit inside the camera and detaching this piece could permanently damage your camera .

Lines.Text: it's important to recognize that this is a camera produced by a japanese camera manufacturer . the japanese camera industry loves using ( japanese industrial standard ) screws .

don't be tempted by your phillips screwdriver collection . although 00 will interchange with jis00 , it is not a perfect fit . using phillips will cause more wear on the head of the jis screws and cause the screws to prematurely strip .
have both jis00 and jis000 screwdrivers available for this teardown . luckily , both bits are included in the 64 bit kit .

Steps.Text_raw: It's important to recognize that this is a camera produced by a Japanese camera manufacturer. The Japanese camera industry loves using [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Industrial_Standards|JIS] (Japanese Industrial Standard) screws. Don't be tempted by your Phillips screw driver collection. Although PH#00 will interchange with JIS#00, it is not a perfect fit. Using Phillips will cause more wear on the head of the JIS screws and cause the screws to prematurely strip. Have both JIS#00 and JIS#000 screw drivers available for this teardown. Luckily, both bits are included in the [https://www.ifixit.com/Store/Tools/64-Bit-Driver-Kit/IF145-299-1|ifixit 64bit kit].

Lines.Text: unscrew the six 4.0 mm jis00 screws on the bottom of the camera . you should now be able to remove the bottom plate from the camera .

Steps.Text_raw: Unscrew the six 4.0 mm JIS#00 screws on the bottom of the camera. You should now be able to remove the bottom plate from the camera.

Lines.Text: get your picks ready !
to get any deeper into this camera , the right-hand port cover assembly must be removed first . once this is removed , you will have access to the screws that secure the other components .
there's a tiny hole toward the bottom right of the battery compartment . using the pick tool , press into that hole .
a plastic rod will release . that plastic rod is the axis the hinge rotates about .

Steps.Text_raw: Get your picks ready! To get any deeper into this camera, the right-hand port cover assembly must be removed first. Once this is removed, you will have access to the screws that secure the other components. There's a tiny hole toward the bottom right of the battery compartment. Using the pick tool, press into that hole. A plastic rod will release. That plastic rod is the axis the hinge rotates about.

Lines.Text: fuji ! what did we tell you about hiding screws behind closed doors ! that's pretty under the table fuji . don't do it again . promise ?
the devil's in the details with this camera . slide the port cover off the hinge rod .
using a pair of pliers , pull the rod out of the top plate of the camera . now you'll have access to the port flap spring .

Steps.Text_raw: Fuji! What did we tell you about hiding screws behind closed doors! That's pretty under the table Fuji. Don't do it again. Promise? The devil's in the details with this camera. Slide the port cover off the hinge rod. Using a pair of pliers, pull the rod out of the top plate of the camera. Now you'll have access to the port flap spring.

Lines.Text: with the port flap removed you can put your screwdriver away . focus on that metal clip looking piece
this metal clip is what provides the spring action to the port flap door . overtime , it receeds further into the camera body , reducing the spring tension on the port flap door .
to put more spring action into that door , simply pry a bit up on that metal clip . pry up , in the direction orthogonal to the camera ,
pull up lightly . don't go crazy and pull too hard , as that metal clip can break from being over stressed . be generous and take your time .
you do not need to remove the entire port flap assembly , like in the last 2 photos of this step . it is unnecessary .

Steps.Text_raw: With the port flap removed you can put your screwdriver away. Focus on that metal clip looking piece This metal clip is what provides the spring action to the port flap door. Overtime, it receeds further into the camera body, reducing the spring tension on the port flap door. To put more spring action into that door, simply pry a bit up on that metal clip. Pry up, in the direction orthogonal to the camera, [http://physicsed.buffalostate.edu/SeatExpts/resource/rhr/rhr.htm|out-of-the-page]. Pull up lightly. Don't go crazy and pull too hard, as that metal clip can break from being over stressed. Be generous and take your time. You do not need to remove the entire port flap assembly, like in the last 2 photos of this step. It is unnecessary.

Lines.Text: locate all of the cables attached to the motherboard .
carefully disconnect all cables .
there are four orange no-fuss ribbon connectors . to disconnect these cables pull up on the tabs protruding from both sides of the cable rather than pulling on the cable itself .
there are two white no-fuss ribbon cable connectors . to disconnect these cables , pull them straight out of the connector .
in the lower corner on the far right , disconnect the zero-insertion force ( zif ) connector by flipping up the small black bar before removing the cable .

Steps.Text_raw: Locate all of the cables attached to the motherboard. Carefully disconnect all cables. There are four orange no-fuss ribbon connectors. To disconnect these cables pull up on the tabs protruding from both sides of the cable rather than pulling on the cable itself. There are two white no-fuss ribbon cable connectors. To disconnect these cables, pull them straight out of the connector. In the lower corner on the far right, disconnect the Zero-Insertion Force (ZIF) connector by flipping up the small black bar before removing the cable. Power Cable: Disconnect the bundled cable connector by prying up gently from the edges.  If you need to,  collect the cables between you fingers and pull gently to remove. Try not to pull more on one wire than the rest as this can strain and separate the wires.

Lines.Text: begin by removing the 5 screws ( located : 2 screws on either side and 1 screw on the bottom ) using the 000 head in the precision phillips screwdriver .

these screws are very small . to keep from losing any pieces , place all small metals on a magnetic project mat .

Steps.Text_raw: Begin by removing the 5 screws (located: 2 screws on either side and 1 screw on the bottom) using the PH000 head in the Precision Phillips Screwdriver. Lines.Text: using your hands or an opening tool , pry off the silver frame , taking special care at the top of the camera where the buttons are as it is a little harder to pry off .

Steps.Text_raw: Using your hands or an opening tool, pry off the silver frame, taking special care at the top of the camera where the buttons are as it is a little harder to pry off. If the back casing is loose from the camera body, it may be easier to perform step 4 first, then accomplish this step. Proceed as your unit allows.

Lines.Text: the last part of the casing to disconnect is the back that houses the lcd screen .
the screen is attached by a connection ribbon . gently pull the casing and screen away from the camera body to disconnect the casing .
the lcd screen is held onto the back casing by a small amount of adhesive . this may come loose during this process . do not worry if they become separated .
this plug and the connection ribbon are fragile , try not to tear the connection ribbon when disconnecting .

Steps.Text_raw: The last part of the casing to disconnect is the back that houses the LCD screen. The screen is attached by a connection ribbon. Gently pull the casing and screen away from the camera body to disconnect the casing. The LCD screen is held onto the back casing by a small amount of adhesive. This may come loose during this process. Do not worry if they become separated. This plug and the connection ribbon are fragile, try not to tear the connection ribbon when disconnecting.

Lines.Text: with the back casing that you just separated from the camera , use your finger to push the lcd screen from the frame .
the lcd screen is secured to the frame with a thin layer of adhesive , not much force is required to removed the screen from the back casing .
before replacing the back casing with the new lcd screen , please be sure it is secured into the casing with new adhesive .

Steps.Text_raw: With the back casing that you just separated from the camera, use your finger to push the LCD screen from the frame. using a phillips 000 screwdriver , remove the four 2-mm screws from the side of the camera .
remove the two 3-mm screws from the other side of the camera .

Lines.Text: the hand strap can become a hindrance at times . it's best to begin by unlatching it .
on the padded section of the hand strap , pry up the velcro and peel out the thin strap sandwiched between them .
push the thin strap through the metal loop at the front of the device .
the strap will still be connected at one end to the device , but will be able to be moved out of the way to provide a more stable working surface .

Steps.Text_raw: The  hand strap can become a hindrance at times. It's best to begin by unlatching it. The strap will still be connected at one end to the device, but will be able to be moved out of the way to provide a more stable working surface.

Lines.Text: flip open the lcd screen and find the screw located above the micro usb port .
remove the screw ( 4 mm , phillips 00 )
using a spudger , or another small plastic prying tool , pop up the silver panel .
it may also help to flip up the sd card cover and tug gently on that piece to assist in prying up the panel .

Steps.Text_raw: Flip open the LCD screen and find the screw located above the micro USB port. It may also help to flip up the SD card cover and tug gently on that piece to assist in prying up the panel.

Lines.Text: once the silver cover is pried up , slip the piece out to the right .
there are two cables attached to the board beneath that need to be disconnected .
disconnect both of the no-fuss ribbon cables .
use your fingernails or a pair of tweezers to pull on the tabs on either side of the ribbon cable to remove .
remove the other cable by pulling up on the cable itself .
''remember : cables are very fragile , be as delicate as you can removing and connecting them . ''

Steps.Text_raw: Once the silver cover is pried up, slip the piece out to the right. There are two cables attached to the board beneath that need to be disconnected. Remove the other cable by pulling up on the cable itself. ''Remember: cables are very fragile, be as delicate as you can removing and connecting them.''

Lines.Text: locate the screw ( phillips 00 ) found in the top right corner of the housing .
remove the screw .

Steps.Text_raw: Locate the screw (Phillips #00) found in the top right corner of the housing. Remove the screw.

Lines.Text: close the lcd screen and turn the device over .
insert your spudger or other plastic pry tool into the small gap between the device housing and the door .
''it's best to do it just above where the word 'close' is printed as that is where the locking mechanism is located within . ''
pry open the door with the spudger , using your other hand to tug the door as you work it open .
''caution : this has the potential to damage the plastic piece that locks the door into place . ''

Steps.Text_raw: Close the LCD screen and turn the device over. Insert your spudger or other plastic pry tool into the small gap between the device housing and the door. ''It's best to do it just above where the word 'close' is printed as that is where the locking mechanism is located within.'' Lines.Text: once the disc door is open , locate the screw ( phillips 00 ) on the inside , top right corner , closest to the camcorder lens .
remove the screw .

Steps.Text_raw: Once the disc door is open, locate the screw (Phillips #00) on the inside, top right corner, closest to the camcorder lens. Remove the screw.

Lines.Text: turn to view the bottom of the device and locate the four screws on the bottom ( 4 mm , phillips 00 ) .
remove all four screws .

Steps.Text_raw: Turn to view the bottom of the device and locate the four screws on the bottom (4mm, Phillips #00). Remove all four screws.

Lines.Text: with the screws removed , the black and silver housing pieces should be able to shift apart from one another .

''caution : do not pull the device apart willy-nilly . there is an internal ribbon cable attached to both halves of the housing that can easily be damaged by doing so . slow and steady wins the race . ''
gently work the black and silver housing pieces away from one another .
''if the housing is a bit resistant to separating , it may help to use a pry tool along the bottom of the device where the two colors meet . ''

Steps.Text_raw: With the screws removed, the black and silver housing pieces should be able to shift apart from one another. ''Caution: do not pull the device apart willy-nilly. There is an internal ribbon cable attached to both halves of the housing that can easily be damaged by doing so. Slow and steady wins the race. '' Gently work the black and silver housing pieces away from one another. ''If the housing is a bit resistant to separating, it may help to use a pry tool along the bottom of the device where the two colors meet.''

Lines.Text: once the device is open , carefully remove the no-fuss ribbon cable from the motherboard and set aside the silver portion of the device .
there may be a piece of plastic adhesive shielding the motherboard . remove gently , being careful not to pull on the ribbon cables beneath it , and set aside .

Steps.Text_raw: Once the device is open, carefully remove the no-fuss ribbon cable from the motherboard and set aside the silver portion of the device. There may be a piece of plastic adhesive shielding the motherboard. Remove gently, being careful not to pull on the ribbon cables beneath it, and set aside.

Lines.Text: locate all of the cables attached to the motherboard .
carefully disconnect all cables .
there are four orange no-fuss ribbon connectors . to disconnect these cables pull up on the tabs protruding from both sides of the cable rather than pulling on the cable itself .
there are two white no-fuss ribbon cable connectors . to disconnect these cables , pull them straight out of the connector .
in the lower corner on the far right , disconnect the zero-insertion force ( zif ) connector by flipping up the small black bar before removing the cable .

power cable : disconnect the bundled cable connector by prying up gently from the edges . if you need to , collect the cables between you fingers and pull gently to remove . try not to pull more on one wire than the rest as this can strain and separate the wires .

Steps.Text_raw: Locate all of the cables attached to the motherboard. Carefully disconnect all cables. There are four orange no-fuss ribbon connectors. To disconnect these cables pull up on the tabs protruding from both sides of the cable rather than pulling on the cable itself. There are two white no-fuss ribbon cable connectors. To disconnect these cables, pull them straight out of the connector. In the lower corner on the far right, disconnect the Zero-Insertion Force (ZIF) connector by flipping up the small black bar before removing the cable. Power Cable: Disconnect the bundled cable connector by prying up gently from the edges.  If you need to,  collect the cables between you fingers and pull gently to remove. Try not to pull more on one wire than the rest as this can strain and separate the wires.

Lines.Text: now that all of the cables are disconnected , remove the two bronze screws ( 2 mm , phillips 00 ) on the lens housing .
next we'll need to remove some screws from inside the disc housing .
if the disc door has closed at some point , turn the camcorder lens toward you and locate a small cylindrical lever to the left of the lens .
pushing down on this lever will manually release the door .

Steps.Text_raw: Now that all of the cables are disconnected, remove the two bronze screws (2mm, Phillips #00) on the lens housing. Next we'll need to remove some screws from inside the disc housing. If the disc door has closed at some point, turn the camcorder lens toward you and locate a small cylindrical lever to the left of the lens. Pushing down on this lever will manually release the door.

Lines.Text: remove the top two upper screws ( 4 mm , phillips 00 ) on the interior of the dvd housing .
pry up the black strip of housing between the open slider and the remaining silver housing above the lens .
a bit of a gentle tug and wiggle of the piece towards the lens side of the device , should allow you to completely remove the piece .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the top two upper screws (4mm, Phillips #00) on the interior of the DVD housing. Pry up the black strip of housing between the open slider and the remaining silver housing above the lens. A bit of a gentle tug and wiggle of the piece towards the lens side of the device, should allow you to completely remove the piece.

Lines.Text: remove the bronze screw ( 2 mm , phillips 00 ) attaching the rear housing to the frame .

if you are using a screwdriver that uses interchangeable tips , the connecting base of the screwdriver is too wide for reaching this screw . you will need to use a standard ( and magnetic , if possible ) phillips 00 screwdriver .
once the screw is removed , the rear housing can be gently pulled away .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the bronze screw (2 mm, Phillips #00) attaching the  rear housing to the frame. If you are using a screwdriver that uses interchangeable tips, the connecting base of the screwdriver is too wide for reaching this screw. You will need to use a standard (and magnetic, if possible) Phillips #00 screwdriver. Once the screw is removed, the rear housing can be gently pulled away.

Lines.Text: with the screw removed , lift up the silver panel above the lens assembly and slide it out towards the lens .
the rear housing should be able to be tugged apart with a small snap .
set aside the rear housing .

Steps.Text_raw: With the screw removed, lift up the silver panel above the lens assembly and slide it out towards the lens. The rear housing should be able to be tugged apart with a small snap. Set aside the rear housing.

Lines.Text: remove the three black screws ( 5 mm , phillips 00 ) connecting the frame to the disc housing .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the three black screws (5 mm, Phillips #00) connecting the  frame to the disc housing.

Lines.Text: remove the motherboard and frame and set aside .
if your replacement part includes the full disc door assembly , you can stop here and reassemble your device .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the motherboard and frame and set aside. If your replacement part includes the full disc door assembly, you can stop here and reassemble your device.

Lines.Text: remove the two outer screws ( 4 mm , phillips 00 ) from the hinge .
opening the door to a full 90 degrees , should allow the door to be tugged up and out from the disc door frame .

Steps.Text_raw: Remove the two outer screws (4mm, Phillips #00) from the hinge. Opening the door to a full 90 degrees,  should allow the door to be tugged up and out from the disc door frame.

Lines.Text: after the door is separated from the frame , set the door aside .
remove the two bronze ( 2 mm , phillips 00 ) screws at the top of the metal frame .
separate the disc reading frame from the optical housing frame and set the disc reading frame aside .

Steps.Text_raw: After the door is separated from the frame, set the door aside. Remove the two bronze (2mm, Phillips #00) screws at the top of the metal frame. Separate the disc reading frame from the optical housing frame and set the disc reading frame aside.

Lines.Text: unscrew the top two screws ( 5 mm , phillips 00 ) on the frame of the optical assembly .
remove the frame from the optical assembly .

Steps.Text_raw: Unscrew the top two screws (5mm, Phillips #00) on the frame of the optical assembly. Remove the frame from the optical assembly.

Lines.Text: you've reached the optical assembly .
depending on the part you've received to replace the optical assembly , you may need to remove the circuit panel on the back of the assembly .
unscrew the two screws ( 5 mm , phillips 00 ) from the circuit board and separate the board from the assembly .

Steps.Text_raw: You've reached the optical assembly. Depending on the part you've received to replace the optical assembly, you may need to remove the circuit panel on the back of the assembly. Unscrew the two screws (5mm, Phillips #00) from the circuit board and separate the board from the assembly.

there are two cables attached to the board beneath that need to be disconnected .
disconnect both of the no-fuss ribbon cables .
use your fingernails or a pair of tweezers to pull on the tabs on either side of the ribbon cable to remove .
remove the other cable by pulling up on the cable itself .
''remember : cables are very fragile , be as delicate as you can removing and connecting them . ''

remove the screw .

Lines.Text: close the lcd screen and turn the device over .
insert your spudger or other plastic pry tool into the small gap between the device housing and the door .
''it's best to do it just above where the word 'close' is printed as that is where the locking mechanism is located within . ''
pry open the door with the spudger , using your other hand to tug the door as you work it open .
''caution : this has the potential to damage the plastic piece that locks the door into place . ''

''It's best to do it just above where the word 'close' is printed as that is where the locking mechanism is located within.'' Pry open the door with the spudger, using your other hand to tug the door as you work it open. ''Caution: this has the potential to damage the plastic piece that locks the door into place.''

Lines.Text: once the disc door is open , locate the screw ( phillips 00 ) on the inside , top right corner , closest to the camcorder lens .
remove the screw .

Lines.Text: turn to view the bottom of the device and locate the four screws on the bottom ( 4 mm , phillips 00 ) .
remove all four screws .

Steps.Text_raw: Turn to view the bottom of the device and locate the four screws on the bottom (4mm, Phillips #00). Remove all four screws.

Lines.Text: with the screws removed , the black and silver housing pieces should be able to shift apart from one another .

''caution : do not pull the device apart willy-nilly . there is an internal ribbon cable attached to both halves of the housing that can easily be damaged by doing so . slow and steady wins the race . ''
gently work the black and silver housing pieces away from one another .
''if the housing is a bit resistant to separating , it may help to use a pry tool along the bottom of the device where the two colors meet . ''

'' Gently work the black and silver housing pieces away from one another. ''If the housing is a bit resistant to separating, it may help to use a pry tool along the bottom of the device where the two colors meet.''

Lines.Text: once the device is open , carefully remove the no-fuss ribbon cable from the motherboard and set aside the silver portion of the device .
there may be a piece of plastic adhesive shielding the motherboard . remove gently , being careful not to pull on the ribbon cables beneath it , and set aside .

Steps.Text_raw: Once the device is open, carefully remove the no-fuss ribbon cable from the motherboard and set aside the silver portion of the device. There may be a piece of plastic adhesive shielding the motherboard. Remove gently, being careful not to pull on the ribbon cables beneath it, and set aside.

Lines.Text: locate all of the cables attached to the motherboard .
carefully disconnect all cables .
there are four orange no-fuss ribbon connectors . to disconnect these cables pull up on the tabs protruding from both sides of the cable rather than pulling on the cable itself .
there are two white no-fuss ribbon cable connectors . to disconnect these cables , pull them straight out of the connector .
in the lower corner on the far right , disconnect the zero-insertion force ( zif ) connector by flipping up the small black bar before removing the cable .

power cable : disconnect the bundled cable connector by prying up gently from the edges . if you need to , collect the cables between you fingers and pull gently to remove . try not to pull more on one wire than the rest as this can strain and separate the wires .

Steps.Text_raw: Locate all of the cables attached to the motherboard. Carefully disconnect all cables. There are four orange no-fuss ribbon connectors. To disconnect these cables pull up on the tabs protruding from both sides of the cable rather than pulling on the cable itself. There are two white no-fuss ribbon cable connectors. To disconnect these cables, pull them straight out of the connector. In the lower corner on the far right, disconnect the Zero-Insertion Force (ZIF) connector by flipping up the small black bar before removing the cable. Power Cable: Disconnect the bundled cable connector by prying up gently from the edges.  If you need to,  collect the cables between you fingers and pull gently to remove. Try not to pull more on one wire than the rest as this can strain and separate the wires.

Lines.Text: now that all of the cables are disconnected , remove the two bronze screws ( 2 mm , phillips 00 ) on the lens housing .
next we'll need to remove some screws from inside the disc housing .
if the disc door has closed at some point , turn the camcorder lens toward you and locate a small cylindrical lever to the left of the lens .
pushing down on this lever will manually release the door .

pry up the black strip of housing between the open slider and the remaining silver housing above the lens .
a bit of a gentle tug and wiggle of the piece towards the lens side of the device , should allow you to completely remove the piece .

once the screw is removed , the rear housing can be gently pulled away .

set aside the rear housing .

opening the door to a full 90 degrees , should allow the door to be tugged up and out from the disc door frame .

Lines.Text: the last part of the casing to disconnect is the back that houses the lcd screen .

this plug and the connection ribbon are fragile , try not to tear the connection ribbon when disconnecting .

Title: Repair LCD screen

Lines.Text: this model does not have a viewfinder and requires the lcd display to take pictures , so trouble shooting is difficult .

turn the knob to auto mode and make sure the shutter is not stuck . take a few test pictures while looking into the lens so you can see whether the shutter closes and opens . also zoom in and zoom out to check if the aperture opens and closes .
next , test the zoom lens is working and the mechanism is moving smoothly - without catching or grinding . the zoom can be knocked crooked , and can be very gently pushed back into place .

Steps.Text_raw: This model does not have a viewfinder and requires the LCD display to take pictures, so trouble shooting is difficult. Turn the knob to "Auto" mode and make sure the shutter is not stuck. Take a few test pictures while looking INTO the lens so you can see whether the shutter closes and opens.  Also Zoom in and zoom out to check if the aperture  opens and closes. Next, test the zoom lens is working and the mechanism is moving smoothly - without catching or grinding. The zoom can be knocked crooked, and can be very gently pushed back into place.

Lines.Text: next , press the menu button on the back of the camera and listen for the typical change in sound . move the selection buttons and listen for the beeps to ensure the options are changing ( since you can't see it on screen ) .

press the shutter button to make sure the camera can take pictures . since the screen is not working , just listen for the proper timing and sounds ( does the auto focus work ? does the red light come on/off on ? does it beep once the auto focus is complete ? )

Steps.Text_raw: Next, press the MENU button on the back of the camera and listen for the typical change in sound. Move the selection buttons and listen for the beeps to ensure the options are changing (since you can't see it on screen). Press the shutter button to make sure the camera can take pictures.  Since the screen is not working, just listen for the proper timing and sounds (does the auto focus work? does the red light come on/off on? Does it beep once the auto focus is complete?)

Lines.Text: turn off camera and connect via usb cable . make sure the camera is charged sufficiently so that it doesn't shut off .

turn on the camera and wait for the computer to recognize it as a new device . explore the image files from the directory to make sure that the previous test shots you made are saving . if the pictures are there , then you know the camera works .

if there is no memory card , delete the photos from the dcim file on your computer , and take more test shots . the camera has limited internal memory and might not capture shots if the memory is already full .

Steps.Text_raw: Turn off camera and connect via USB cable. Make sure the camera is charged sufficiently so that it doesn't shut off. Turn on the camera and wait for the computer to recognize it as a new device.   Explore the image files from the directory to make sure that the previous test shots you made are saving. If the pictures are there, then you know the camera works. If there is no Memory Card, delete the photos from the DCIM file on your computer, and take more test shots. The camera has limited internal memory and might not capture shots if the memory is already full.

Lines.Text: check to see flat cable is loose at the base on the metal arms . if the ldc screen is disconnected , this will be loose or sticking out . otherwise , you should only see it coming out the back of the lcd screen .

use phillips screwdriver to remove the plate over the cable and the screws on the bottom left and bottom right corners of the arm . keep track of screws , the ones connecting the arms to the camera body will be market with blue/color .
once arm is removed , remove the screws around the lcd screen to take apart the assembly . this image is not the exact model but it helped me take the lcd assembly apart .

Lines.Text: you need tweezers , very bright light and magnifying glass to reconnect the cable . test to see if screen works , does it light up ( if cable is installed upside down , the screen will light up but not show images ) .

if the screen does light up , start reassembling the entire lcd mechanism . turn off camera and ( 1 ) connect the arms back onto the camera body , making sure to place flat cable through the slot in the lcd frame .

(2 ) there will be very little room to connect the cable , use the magnifier and light see clearly , and use the tweezers to push the cable connection firmly into the slot on the back of the interior lcd screen .

(3 ) turn on the camera to test if the screen is working properly . this step took a few tries before the display worked properly , so try it several times ! the connector must be inserted fully and evenly otherwise the screen will light up , but no image will be shown .

Steps.Text_raw: You need tweezers, very bright light and magnifying glass to reconnect the cable.  TEST TO SEE IF SCREEN WORKS, does it light up (if cable is installed upside down, the screen will light up but not show images). If the screen DOES light up, start reassembling the entire LCD mechanism.  TURN OFF camera and (1) Connect the arms back onto the camera body, making sure to place flat cable through the slot in the LCD frame. (2) There will be very little room to connect the cable, use the magnifier and light see clearly, and use the tweezers to push the cable connection firmly into the slot on the back of the interior LCD screen. (3) TURN ON the camera to test if the screen is working properly. This step took a few tries before the display worked properly, so try it several times! The connector must be inserted fully and evenly otherwise the screen will light up, but no image will be shown.

Lines.Text: once the screen is showing the current images , use a sticker or adhesive to the exposed portion of the flat cable . if this gets pulled loose , you have to start over again . replace flat plate over the cable to hold it in place .

final step is to replace and tighten all of the screws on the exterior lcd screen housing and attached to camera body , especially in the corners . from there , everything should work as normal : ) ) )

Steps.Text_raw: Once the screen is showing the current images, use a sticker or adhesive to the exposed portion of the flat cable. If this gets pulled loose, you have to start over again.  Replace flat plate over the cable to hold it in place. Final step is to replace and tighten all of the screws on the exterior LCD screen housing and attached to camera body, especially in the corners.  From there, everything should work as normal :)))

Lines.Text: if required , you can now lift out the lens assembly .
if you suspect dust or contamination on the sensor or ir filter you can go on from this stage to clean them without removing the lens .

the symptoms are one or more dark patches at the same place in all images and at all levels of optical zoom , but getting bigger and possibly moving out of the image on digital zoom . if the patches are fuzzy then the contamination is probably on the ir filter but if well defined , it's more likely on the sensor itself .

a video at shows the procedure for a different but similar model of lumix camera . one difference is that you will need a small torx rather than cross-head screwdriver ( i think t4 or maybe t3 but unfortunately i forgot to make a note of which ) .

Steps.Text_raw: If required, you can now lift out the lens assembly. If you suspect dust or contamination on the sensor or IR filter you can go on from this stage to clean them without removing the lens. The symptoms are one or more dark patches at the same place in all images and at all levels of optical zoom, but getting bigger and possibly moving out of the image on digital zoom. If the patches are fuzzy then the contamination is probably on the IR filter but if well defined, it's more likely on the sensor itself. A video at https://youtu.be/0nmwt0frZns shows the procedure for a different but similar model of Lumix camera. One difference is that you will need a small Torx rather than cross-head screwdriver (I think T4 or maybe T3 but unfortunately I forgot to make a note of which). With the lens removed you may be able to test the zoom by applying a 3V battery to the terminals on the bottom of the zoom motor, which is mounted on the side of the lens. Reverse the polarity of the battery to reverse the direction of motion.

Title: Fujifilm FinePix Z1 LCD Screen Replacement

Lines.Text: ensure that the camera is charged and not on powersave mode .

if the camera is charged and on , a faulty lcd screen could be caused by a scratch or water damage . also , trauma to the camera could cause the screen to shatter . in any of these cases , the screen will need to be replaced .
make sure that the orange thin cable is appropriately attached .

Steps.Text_raw: Ensure that the camera is charged and not on PowerSave mode. If the camera is charged and on, a faulty LCD Screen could be caused by a scratch or water damage. Also, trauma to the camera could cause the screen to shatter. In any of these cases, the screen will need to be replaced. Make sure that the orange thin cable is appropriately attached.

Lines.Text: open the camera by removing the 5 external 4.0 mm screws with the 1.0 flathead .

Steps.Text_raw: Open the camera by removing the 5 external 4.0 mm screws with the 1.0 flathead.

Lines.Text: gently pull the components apart .
remove the 2.0 mm screw to the left of the sd card .
the lcd screen is located on the back of the circuit board and can be accessed after removing the internal components .

Steps.Text_raw: Gently pull the components apart. Remove the 2.0mm screw to the left of the SD card. The LCD screen is located on the back of the circuit board and can be accessed after removing the internal components.

Lines.Text: use the 00 to pry open the display screen of the camera .
expose the display screen and make sure the cable connecting the screen and the camera are separated . remember where the cable connection is located to attach the replacement screen .
use the to solder and desolder connections guide to remove the screen from the device .

Steps.Text_raw: Use the PH00 to pry open the display screen of the camera. Expose the display screen and make sure the cable connecting the screen and the camera are separated. Remember where the cable connection is located to attach the replacement screen. Use the [https://www.ifixit.com/Guide/How+To+Solder+and+Desolder+Connections/750|How to Solder and Desolder Connections Guide] to remove the screen from the device.

Lines.Text: find the front face of the camera and test to see of the lens barrier will slide .
make sure items are not trapped or stuck between the lens barrier and the camera lens .
check to see if the camera power turns on by sliding the barrier . if not check to see if the lens barrier is on the correct track .

Steps.Text_raw: Find the front face of the camera and test to see of the Lens Barrier will slide. Make sure items are not trapped or stuck between the Lens Barrier and the camera lens. Check to see if the camera power turns on by sliding the barrier. If not check to see if the lens barrier is on the correct track.

make sure the circular spring on the back of the door is intact by manoeuvring the lens barrier and finding the sticking point .

Lines.Text: find the thin , flat orange cable connector that operates the lens barrier and connects it to the main circuit board .
check to make sure the cable is not stuck or broken .

Steps.Text_raw: Find the thin, flat orange cable connector that operates the lens barrier and connects it to the main circuit board. Check to make sure the cable is not stuck or broken.

this last step will require you to solder some of the cable connectors . click to learn how to complete this step .
